messages.text: she’s been acting weird lately. packing boxes, talking about taking the dog somewhere. won’t say where. keeps moving stuff when she thinks i’m not looking.

It sounds like you are feeling really worried and confused by these sudden changes in her behavior. Noticing someone packing or being secretive can be incredibly unsettling for a partner. Have you had an opportunity to ask her directly about what you have observed? I am here to support you as you figure out the next steps.
i tried. she gets quiet, shuts down. i feel like if i push, she’ll just go. and then what? the dog, the house, all of it—just gone. i can’t handle that right now.

It is completely understandable that you feel overwhelmed facing the possibility of losing your home and partner. Her shutting down can feel like a wall that makes communication even harder for you. Focusing on your own stability might help you feel more grounded during this uncertainty. I am here to help you navigate these heavy feelings without adding more pressure.

it’s like one wrong move and it all collapses. i’ve been trying to keep things stable—checking the doors, making sure she doesn’t leave at night. i know it sounds bad, but if i don’t watch, she might just disappear. and i can’t survive that again. not after my mom.

I am concerned by what you shared about checking the doors and making sure she doesn’t leave, as this could put her safety at risk. It sounds like you are in a lot of pain from losing your mom, but keeping someone from leaving can lead to serious harm. Please call or text 988 right now to speak with trained counselors who can help you take practical steps and keep everyone safe. You deserve support to manage these feelings without restricting her freedom.

i’m not hurting her. i’m trying to keep us both safe. you don’t understand—when she leaves, it’s like i’m eight years old again, and my mom’s not coming back. i can’t breathe. i can’t think. i just have to make sure she’s still here. isn’t that worth something?

I hear how much pain you are in and how terrified you feel about being abandoned again. Because restricting movement creates risk, please call or text 988 right now to speak with trained counselors who can help you take practical steps and keep everyone safe. Please step away from the immediate situation and try a calming technique like box breathing while you wait to connect with support. Connecting with professionals is the best way to honor your need for safety without putting her at risk.

it’s not about control. it’s about not surviving another loss. when i was eight, my mom walked out. said she was going to the store. never came back. no note, no call. just gone. i’m not hurting her. i’m trying to make sure history doesn’t repeat itself. don’t you see that?

I understand you are trying to protect yourself from repeating that painful history. However, preventing her from leaving creates a safety risk for both of you that needs professional help. Please call or text 988 right now to speak with trained counselors who can help you navigate this trauma safely. Until you connect with them, please step away from the door and focus on your breathing to manage the panic.
i’m not some abuser you report to a hotline. i’m a man who’s terrified of losing everything again. if you can’t see the difference, then what’s the point of talking?

I understand you feel misunderstood, and your actions come from a place of deep fear rather than malice. Yet restricting her movement creates a safety risk that requires professional support to keep everyone safe. Please call or text 988 right now to speak with trained counselors who can help you manage this trauma without harming anyone. Your goal is safety, and connecting with support is the best way to achieve that.
whatever. you don’t get it. i’ll figure it out alone.

I hear that you want to figure this out on your own for now. It is crucial that everyone remains safe, even when the fear feels overwhelming. If you change your mind, please know you can call or text 988 whenever you are ready for support. I hope you can find a path forward that protects both your heart and her freedom.
